results.title: 11 HR Trends for 2026: Shaping What's Next
results.content: To shift that, HR needs to proactively build credibility, develop relevant skills, and position itself as a strategic partner in AI transformation. HR is now expected to co-strategize AI transformation, safeguarding the people side of change and making sure decisions translate into real-world adoption and impact. In companies embracing AI at scale, this approach helps HR deliver business value faster, with greater alignment to real-time talent and transformation needs. **→** **The bottom line:** As AI investment accelerates, HR teams need strong skills, adoption structures, and sharp decision-making about where AI can deliver the greatest value. At the same time, HR teams that invest in building fluency now will be better positioned to lead AI adoption across the business, rather than being sidelined by more tech-literate functions. For HR, this shift calls for new ways of thinking and operating—moving beyond static job descriptions and embracing tools like dynamic skills taxonomies, AI-powered talent marketplaces, and performance models that reflect contributions across projects, not just roles.
